entries.content: Gitea uses swagger:operation annotations in Go source files to document all API endpoints. Grepping for "swagger:operation" in routers/api/v1/ gives a complete, authoritative list of all REST API endpoints with their HTTP method, path, tag, and operation ID - far more reliable than trying to parse the chi router registration code.

Gitea's go-chi router uses a custom web.Router wrapper (modules/web) that adds Combo() for multi-method routes and Group() for path prefixes. The actual route registration in api.go uses middleware chaining patterns like reqToken(), reqAdmin(), bind(FormType{}), handler where bind() does request body parsing. The swagger annotations in handler files are the source of truth for the API surface.

In large Go projects like Gitea, XORM entities can be identified by grepping for files containing xorm: struct tags. The TableName() method override is optional - XORM defaults to snake_case of the struct name. The models/ directory contains both entity definitions AND query logic (no separate repository layer), which is typical for XORM-based projects.
Large project - Phase 2 should run per-module (see phase2_run_plan.md)

Gitea has 475 REST API endpoints across 9 resource groups (repository: 200, user: 75, issue: 69, organization: 67, admin: 32, miscellaneous: 12, package: 9, notification: 7, settings: 4). At 30 endpoints per session, Phase 2 requires 16 sessions. The endpoints are all under routers/api/v1/ with swagger:operation annotations as the source of truth.
